title.narrative: Output 6.4. Increased capacity of Member States to strengthen legislation, polices and measures to ensure equal opportunities and treatment in the world of work for persons with disabilities and other persons in vulnerable situations

description.narrative: Migrants: • A total of 132,177 migrant and industrial workers were reached out of which 84 percent were males and 16 percent were females. About half of these were migrant workers. • A total of 33178 (25 percent of those reached) volunteered to take an HIV test. Out of these 87 percent were males and 13 percent were females. • The majority - 75 percent - were first-time testers. Also, 73 percent of those who took a test were between 25 and 35 years of age. • A total of 99 workers tested positive for HIV and were linked with the government’s treatment programme. • A total of 2291 workers were registered in social protection schemes meant for informal economy workers. • As for other services, 37 workers were treated for reproductive tract infections / sexually transmitted infections; 161 were referred to TB screening out of which 20 were confirmed with TB infection and were put on treatment. • As a major part of the intervention covered the period of COVID-19, workers were also provided with COVID-19 prevention messages. Close to 20,050 face masks were distributed and workers were also provided access to approved medication. Skilling: - 449 persons were identified and provided skill-building training in different trades/courses - Out of 449, 216 are HIV positive and 233 are members of HIV-infected families - 13 trades/courses identified by GSNP+ for the training - 113 trained persons were linked to employment with the help of chambers of commerce and diamond associations at Surat, Gujarat Disability-inclusion: 11 persons with disabilities identified from rural areas and trained as Disability Inclusion Facilitators (DIFs) to promote disability inclusion approachesn in Washim, Maharashtra state. Migrants: Under joint UN action, ILO collaborated with Gujarat State AIDS Control Society (GSACS), a state government body, and Gujarat AIDS Prevention (GAP), a civil society organization to reach out to migrant and informal workers with a package of services that includes awareness on HIV and TB, provision of HIV and TB screening at workplace and linking of eligible workers with social protection schemes of state and central government. HIV testing at worksites, focusing on migrant and industrial workers, can reduce HIV testing gaps amongst men. The ILO contributed to the test and treat objective of the National AIDS Control Programme and proved to be a good model of reducing the HIV testing gap amongst men by engaging multi-stakeholders such as industries, unions, and industrial associations. Skilling: ILO collaborated with Gujarat state network of positive people (GSNP+) for skill building programme of women and youth infected or affected by HIV. Under this intervention, , GSNP+ has identified 449 person (267 youth, 129 women, 37 members from LGBTIQ community and 16 were female sex workers). All are members of GSNP+) either infected or affected by HIV. A series of workshops were organized to identify existing skills and interests for training and livelihood. Disability-inclusion: ILO, with funding from IFAD, partnered with Mahila Arthik Vikas Mahamandal to mainstream disability Inclusion in Washim District of Maharashtra.
